summary: Charles Augustus Kincaid was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Sherborne School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1889–1891).

Charles B. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner in 1996 and later served as Associate Professor and Associate Dean at the Catholic University of America.

Linguist Charles Bally studied at the University of Geneva and Humboldt University of Berlin, and was a student of Ferdinand de Saussure. He served as Professor of Greek at Collège Calvin (1900–1913) and as Privatdozent at the University of Geneva (1893–1939).
Charles Barbier de Meynard was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied under Julius Mohl. He was attested as a member of the Institut de France in 1894.
Charles Bowles was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Succeeding John Shakespear, he served as Professor of Hindustani at Addiscombe Military Seminary from around 1836 to 1861.

Indologist Charles Bruce studied at Yale, Westminster, Harrow, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. His positions included Assistant Librarian at the British Museum Library, unpaid Professor of Sanskrit at King's College London (1865–1869), and posts in Mauritius and the UK Government.

Charles Burnett is a historian and philosopher who earned his degrees at the University of Cambridge. He held fellowships at St John's College, Sheffield, and the IAS, and served as Professor at the University of London and the Warburg Institute.
Indologist Charles Chapman studied at Hoxton Academy and under the traditional teacher Mahesha. He was a founder of The Asiatic Society.

Charles Cutler Torrey worked in religious studies, history, and linguistics after studying under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900), founded ASOR in 1901, and served as Professor at Yale University (1900–1932).

Charles D. Orzech, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies and Sinology, earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at UNC Greensboro and was a fellow at the National Humanities Center (2009–2010).

Charles DiSimone, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, completed his PhD at the University of Munich by 2016. He later held posts at the University of Munich (attested 2021) and Ghent University as co-director and permanent member (attested 2026).

Charles Duroiselle worked in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940) and Burma Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India, and was Professor at the University of Rangoon (~1920–1924).

Charles Edmund Godakumbura studied at Kingswood College, Sangaraja Pirivena, and the University of London (PhD 1945, DLitt 1954). He served as Senior Lecturer at the University of London/SOAS and Commissioner of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1956–1967).

Charles Egbert Kennet was a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Bishop's College, Calcutta. He served as teacher (1872) and Principal (1877) at Madras Theological College and became a Fellow at the University of Madras (~1877–1884).

Charles Eliot studied at Cheltenham College and Balliol College, Oxford, working in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served in the Foreign Office and held posts as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sheffield (~1905–1912) and the University of Hong Kong (1912–1918).
Indology scholar Charles Elliott studied at Fort William College (~1801–1803). He worked for the East India Company (~1795–1827) and served as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1837–1856).

Charles Evelyn Arbuthnot William Oldham, an Indology and history/archaeology scholar, studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1888–1890). He served as Assistant Editor of the Indian Antiquary (~1923–1931) and Honorary Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1935–1941).

Charles Gabriel Seligman studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School. Active in history and archaeology, he served as Lecturer (1910) and Chair of Ethnology (1913–1934) at the London School of Economics and the University of London.

Charles Georges Marcel Autran was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut Français d'Archéologie Orientale. He served as a Professor at Aix-Marseille University.
Charles Godfrey Chenevix Trench, an Indology and linguistics scholar, earned his B.A. studying at the University of Oxford and Lincoln College between ~1896 and 1900.
